h1: The 5 Best Metal Storage Carts of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Metal Storage Carts: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 5 metal rolling storage carts scored on load rating, wheel locks, basket design and build, from YASONIC to Simple Houseware.
summary: The YASONIC 3 Tier Rolling Cart is the best of the five: all metal, with a stated 110 lb load rating. The Simple Houseware heavy-duty cart is the better choice if you move a loaded cart often, the Rolling Cart with Drawers adds a closed drawer, and the NEWBULIG is the cheapest way into metal baskets with locking wheels.
intro: Rolling carts fail at the wheels, not the frame. A cart with a well-welded steel frame and four cheap casters will wobble within a month once the top basket is loaded, because the load sits high and every threshold bump pushes on a thin axle. That is why the load rating and the caster description matter more than the number of tiers or the color of the finish.

We ranked five all-metal three-tier carts and weighed stated load capacity, wheel design and how the baskets are built. We could only judge what each listing says, so a cart with a published rating beat one with only marketing words. Duplicate listings of the same YASONIC cart were folded into a single entry.

products.name: YASONIC 3 Tier Rolling Cart
products.verdict: A 100% metal cart with a stated 110 lb capacity, the only hard number in this ranking.
products.description:
YASONIC describes this three-tier cart as 100% metal, with a 110 lb load-bearing rating and a coating treated against wear. It is described as moving easily and staying stable under heavy loads, and it sits in the $25 to $50 bucket.

A published rating is what puts it first. Most carts at this price give only adjectives, and 110 lb across three baskets works out to a sensible limit of about 35 lb per tier if spread evenly. It outranks Simple Houseware because the load figure is concrete, though Simple Houseware leans harder on wheel language.

Buy it for a kitchen, laundry or craft room where you want a known limit. The listing says nothing about locking wheels, so check that before you park it on a slope or beside a stove.
products.idealFor: Kitchens and craft rooms that need a known weight limit.
products.skipIf: You must have locking wheels confirmed.

products.name: Simple Houseware 3-Tier Heavy Duty Metal Utility Rolling Cart
products.verdict: Heavy-duty construction, three metal baskets and heavy-duty casters.
products.description:
Simple Houseware builds this cart around heavy-duty construction, three metal baskets and heavy-duty casters. It sits in the $25 to $50 bucket, alongside the YASONIC.

The casters are what earn the second spot. Wheels are the part that fail first on loaded carts, and this listing calls them heavy duty where the others stay vague. It ranks behind the YASONIC only because no load figure is given, so you cannot compare the two on numbers. Against the NEWBULIG it gives up the stated lockable wheels but takes a clearer heavy-duty claim.

Buy it if the cart will be pushed around daily, such as in a garage or workshop. Confirm the casters can lock before relying on it, because the listing does not say.
products.idealFor: Garages and workshops where the cart moves daily.
products.skipIf: You want a published weight limit.

products.name: Rolling Cart with Drawers
products.verdict: A reinforced metal cart with lockable wheels and smooth-glide drawers.
products.description:
This cart is built from reinforced metal, has lockable wheels and uses a smooth-glide drawer design. It sits in the $50 to $100 bucket, the most expensive in this ranking.

The drawers are why it is here. Open baskets leave everything visible, which is fine for towels and pantry cans but poor for small items, and a drawer hides them. The lockable wheels are also a stated safety feature, which the YASONIC lacks. It ranks third because the listing gives no load rating or drawer count, and you pay for the extra construction.

Buy it for a bedroom, bathroom or craft room where items should be out of sight. The missing capacity figure means you should keep the drawers to light contents.
products.idealFor: Rooms where small items should stay out of sight.

products.name: 3 Tier Heavy Duty White Metal Rolling Cart with Lockable Wheels, Roller Cart
products.verdict: A white metal cart with lockable wheels and a large capacity, suited to kitchens and bathrooms.
products.description:
This white three-tier cart is described as heavy duty, comes with lockable wheels and is pitched for a kitchen cart, bathroom or similar use. The listing stresses large capacity and easy movement, and it sits in the $25 to $50 bucket.

The white finish and wheel locks make it the more domestic pick. It suits a bathroom or kitchen where black steel would look heavy. It ranks fourth because 'heavy duty' and 'large capacity' come with no number, the same as the Simple Houseware, and it adds no drawers like the third-place cart.

Buy it where looks and wheel locks matter more than proof of capacity. The white finish may chip in a garage, so use it indoors.
products.idealFor: Kitchens and bathrooms where a white finish fits.
products.skipIf: You will use it in a rough garage.

products.name: NEWBULIG 3-Tier Metal Rolling Storage Utility Cart with Lockable Wheels
products.verdict: Rust-resistant metal, graduated mesh baskets and lockable wheels, in the under $25 bucket.
products.description:
NEWBULIG offers rust-resistant metal, graduated basket sizes, breathable mesh for fresh storage and lockable wheels. It is the only cart in the under $25 bucket.

Graduated baskets are the distinctive feature. A small top basket and larger bottom ones fit a mix of items, such as produce on the bottom and spices on top, and the mesh lets air circulate around onions and potatoes. It ranks last because the listing gives no load rating, and the frame is the least documented of the five.

Buy it for a pantry, kitchen or bathroom on a budget. Because the tiers shrink, the cart holds less than the YASONIC, so avoid heavy cookware.
products.idealFor: Pantries and kitchens on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You plan to load heavy cookware.

whatMatters.detail: Load rating is the total weight a cart is built to carry, and it is the one number that separates a cart from a toy. The YASONIC lists 110 lb. Check whether the listing says total or per tier, and keep the heaviest items on the bottom shelf, since a top-heavy cart tips on a threshold.

Wheels decide whether the cart is useful or a hazard. Locking casters hold it still while you load it, and heavy-duty ones resist the sideways load of a bump. Find the wheel line on the listing and look for both a lock and a size, then check that it rolls on your floor type without catching.

A metal cart can still rust in a damp bathroom or kitchen if the coating is thin. Powder coating and rust-resistant treatments help, but they must be stated. Read the material line on the listing, and be wary of the vague phrase metal-look, which sometimes means plastic baskets on a steel frame, and look for stated rust resistance if the cart will live near water.

Mesh baskets let air circulate, which suits produce, while solid ones stop small items falling through, and drawers hide clutter. The NEWBULIG uses graduated mesh and the Rolling Cart has a drawer. Choose by what you store, and look at the listed dimensions to be sure your largest item fits, with a little clearance so the basket does not bind.

Rolling carts arrive flat and need assembly, and loose bolts are the usual cause of wobble. Allow time for it and tighten everything after a week of use. Check the listing for overall dimensions, and measure the gap where the cart will live, including space to pull it out and turn, since a cart you cannot get out of its corner will stop being used.

faq.q: Do these carts need to be bolted together?
faq.a: Yes. Rolling carts such as the YASONIC and Simple Houseware ship flat and need assembly. Tighten every bolt after the first week, since a loose joint is the most common reason a loaded cart starts to wobble.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with rolling carts?
faq.a: Overloading the top basket. A loaded top makes the cart tip on door thresholds, even with a 110 lb rating like the YASONIC's. Keep heavy items on the bottom and light ones on top.

faq.q: Is the drawer cart worth more than the YASONIC?
faq.a: Only if you need to hide items. The Rolling Cart with Drawers costs more and publishes no load rating, while the YASONIC states 110 lb. For plain storage, the YASONIC is the better value.

faq.q: Can I use a metal cart in a bathroom?
faq.a: Yes, but prefer rust-resistant models. The NEWBULIG states rust-resistant metal and the white cart suits a bathroom's look. Wipe moisture off the frame and avoid leaving the cart in standing water.

faq.q: How do I keep the wheels working?
faq.a: Clear hair and grit from the casters regularly, and check the locks hold. Heavy-duty casters on the Simple Houseware cart cope better with garage dirt, so clean them as part of normal upkeep.
Hard wheels can mark soft flooring. None of the listings describe tire material, so roll the cart gently on hardwood or vinyl, or put a mat down where it parks, especially with locked wheels.

finalTake: For most households the YASONIC 3 Tier Rolling Cart is the right buy, because it is all metal and states a 110 lb capacity. Take the Simple Houseware if the cart will be pushed hard every day, the Rolling Cart with Drawers if you want to hide clutter, and the NEWBULIG if the budget is tight and you want locking wheels.
